title: Treat obesity-associated obstructive sleep apnoea with an approved medicine

concept.text: Reduce clinically significant sleep-disordered breathing pharmacologically in adults with obesity. Tirzepatide achieved an OSA indication following trials both with and without background positive-airway-pressure treatment. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity, supported by randomized trials showing clinically meaningful superiority in apnoea–hypopnoea index at 52 weeks. Test set by: FDA; the two pivotal trials enrolled 469 adults and used change in AHI as the primary efficacy measure. Reported achieved: FDA approved Zepbound for this OSA indication on 20 December 2024. Overlaps: END-05. Sources given: [FDA OSA approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-medication-obstructive-sleep-apnea) ; [Sponsor's indication-specific approval announcement](https://lilly.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fda-approves-zepboundr-tirzepatide-first-and-only-prescription).

page.title: Pharmacotherapy for obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity
page.definition: An FDA-approved medicine reduces breathing interruptions in adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea, repeated upper-airway blockage during sleep. Moderate-to-severe means an apnoea–hypopnoea index (AHI), the number of breathing pauses or reductions per hour of sleep, of at least 15.

goal.need: The global estimates below concern adults aged 30–69 and include all body weights. The American Thoracic Society identifies excess weight as a reversible contributor to OSA severity and recommends incorporating weight management into routine OSA care.

figures.caption: Estimated global prevalence of obstructive sleep apnoea.
figures.note: Published in 2019 using the American Academy of Sleep Medicine’s 2012 scoring criteria.

statements.context: For patients with OSA, body mass index ≥27 kg/m², insufficient weight loss despite comprehensive lifestyle treatment, and no contraindications or active cardiovascular disease.

statements.quote: Today’s approval marks the first drug treatment option for certain patients with obstructive sleep apnea

completion.title: The FDA approves a medicine for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval with an explicit indication to treat moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity. The approved Zepbound indication specifies use with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, approval letter for NDA 217806/S-013 and accompanying prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity.
completion.basis: The capability is an indication-specific authorised treatment, so the regulatory approval is the completion event. Achieved: FDA approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) for this indication on 20 December 2024.

milestones.title: Phentermine/topiramate lowers AHI versus placebo at weeks 8 and 28 in a phase 2 OSA trial.
milestones.criterion: The registered phase 2 protocol tests change in sleep-laboratory AHI at weeks 8 and 28 versus placebo, with lifestyle counselling in both groups. In 45 adults with body mass index 30–40 kg/m² and moderate-to-severe OSA not using positive-airway-pressure (PAP) therapy, phentermine 15 mg/extended-release topiramate 92 mg daily reduced AHI by 31.5 versus 16.6 events/h at week 28 (one-sided P=0.0084); week 8 also favoured treatment (P=0.0009). Published on 1 November 2012.
milestones.set_by: VIVUS and Kentucky Research Group, registered protocol NCT00745251, primary efficacy endpoint published in Sleep. This test is specific to phentermine/topiramate in patients not using PAP.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in AHI between baseline, Week 8, and Week 28 or early withdrawal.

milestones.title: Liraglutide lowers AHI versus placebo at 32 weeks, with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero.
milestones.criterion: The SCALE protocol tests baseline-to-week-32 AHI change with liraglutide 3.0 mg daily versus placebo, using a two-sided 5% test: the 95% confidence interval for the treatment difference excludes zero. Both groups receive diet and exercise. In 359 adults without diabetes, with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA, unable or unwilling to use PAP, reductions were 12.2 versus 6.1 events/h; difference −6.1 (95% CI −11.0 to −1.2), P=0.015. Published on 23 March 2016.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk, SCALE Sleep Apnea protocol NCT01557166, prespecified statistical analysis published in International Journal of Obesity. This test is specific to liraglutide in patients not using PAP.
milestones.threshold_quote: The null hypothesis was rejected on a 5% level if the two-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) of the treatment difference excluded 0.

milestones.title: Tirzepatide lowers AHI versus placebo at 52 weeks in both phase 3 OSA trials at two-sided α=0.05.
milestones.criterion: Each SURMOUNT-OSA trial tests superiority of tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg weekly versus placebo for baseline-to-week-52 polysomnographic AHI change, at two-sided α=0.05; both groups receive lifestyle intervention. The trials randomized 234 adults not using PAP and 235 using PAP. Estimated treatment differences were −20.0 (95% CI −25.8 to −14.2) and −23.8 (−29.6 to −17.9) events/h, respectively; both P<0.001. PAP users suspended therapy for 7 days before assessments. Published on 21 June 2024.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and the SURMOUNT-OSA investigators, master protocol NCT05412004, objectives and statistical analysis published in the design and results papers.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrate the superiority of tirzepatide at the MTD after 52 weeks of treatment, compared with placebo

not_found: Searches for FDA or society preclinical efficacy criteria for obesity-associated OSA found no numerical pass threshold.
The ClinicalTrials.gov page for NCT05412004 did not display its study fields; the published design paper documents the protocol.
The full FDA multidisciplinary review package for NDA 217806/S-013 could not be opened.

results.finding: In 45 adults with OSA and obesity, phentermine/topiramate reduced AHI by 14.9 events/h more than placebo at week 28.
results.detail: Both groups received lifestyle counselling. AHI also favoured treatment at week 8 (P=0.0009). The week 28 analysis used last observation carried forward.
results.quote: The placebo-adjusted LS mean change in AHI at Week 8 was −16.4 (1-sided 95% CI: -∞, −8.14; P = 0.0009) and at Week 28 was −14.9 (LOCF; 1-sided 95% CI: -∞, −4.84; P = 0.0084).

results.finding: In 359 adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA, liraglutide reduced AHI versus placebo by 6.1 events per hour at 32 weeks.
results.detail: The 95% confidence interval for the treatment difference was −11.0 to −1.2 events per hour. Both groups received diet and exercise counseling. The primary analysis used last-observation-carried-forward imputation.
